174	\subsection{Threshold Recommendation}
175	
176	For the main diagnostic (Task~B2), we recommend $\nve \geq 1.5\times$ as the operating threshold for three reasons:
177	
178	\begin{enumerate}[nosep,leftmargin=*]
179	\item \textbf{Maximum recall.} The $1.5\times$ threshold achieves 100\% recall, detecting all four CIVO cases including the transient case (009b, $\nve = 1.62\times$). Raising the threshold to $1.7\times$ loses 009b, dropping recall to 75.0\%.
180	\item \textbf{Best F1.} At $1.5\times$, F1 = 88.9\%, the highest among all tested thresholds for B2. The single false positive (008e\_v3\_s2) is mechanistically identifiable as IRD rather than CIVO.
181	\item \textbf{Sensitivity--specificity tradeoff.} Lower thresholds ($1.0\times$) add false positives without gaining true positives. Higher thresholds ($\geq 1.7\times$) sacrifice recall without eliminating the 008e\_v3\_s2 false positive (which requires $\tau > 3.78$).
182	\end{enumerate}
183	
184	For Task~B1 (sustained CIVO only), perfect classification is achievable at $\nve \geq 3.9\times$, but with only $n_{\text{pos}} = 3$ the statistical power remains limited (accuracy 95\% CI: [69.2\%, 100\%]).
185	
186	\paragraph{Limitations.} With $n = 10$ experiments, Clopper-Pearson confidence intervals remain wide (e.g., 90.0\% accuracy has 95\% CI [55.5\%, 99.7\%]). These results should be interpreted as a diagnostic proof-of-concept rather than a validated clinical threshold. Replication across additional environments and seeds is needed to establish tighter bounds. Table~\ref{tab:sensitivity_b2_full} extends the analysis to the full $n{=}16$ evaluation set spanning both environments, confirming the same operating point ($\nve \geq 1.5\times$, AUROC${=}0.953$).
